claims.text: The initial composite contains discrete W particles or interconnected W ligaments embedded in a Cu matrix.
Untreated W–Cu composites develop phase separation and deleterious interfacial voids under the stated service conditions.
A thin, conformal HEA interlayer should be deposited on W surfaces before W–Cu composite consolidation.
CoCrFeNiCu is a candidate composition for the HEA interlayer.
Electroless plating or sputtering can produce the proposed thin, conformal HEA coating on the W phase before consolidation.
The HEA interlayer will act as a diffusion barrier and interfacial mediator between W and Cu.
The HEA interlayer will create a graded, well-bonded interface between W and Cu.
The graded HEA interface will minimize composition gradients and reduce interfacial void nucleation.
The HEA has good lattice compatibility with the adjoining W and Cu phases.
High mixing entropy and the intermediate HEA phase will modulate interdiffusion during thermal cycling and irradiation.
Modulated interdiffusion will suppress thermodynamically driven phase separation in W–Cu.
The HEA coating will suppress the formation and growth of interfacial voids during thermal cycling and irradiation.
Fewer voids and improved bonding will maintain a continuous, low-resistance heat-flow pathway.
The HEA-coated W–Cu composite will have higher effective thermal conductivity than the untreated composite.
The thermal-conductivity advantage will persist after high-heat-flux and irradiation exposure.
The intervention is applicable under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions characteristic of joints between plasma-facing W materials and Cu-based cooling components.
Performance may be lost at temperatures or irradiation doses beyond typical fusion-joint conditions or if the HEA coating degrades.
The long-term stability of the HEA interlayer under continuous irradiation and extreme thermal cycling is uncertain and depends on coating thickness and composition.
